open_points.subject: A07 operation-node output disclosure
open_points.text: Rule 2 says "for an operation node, the class its binding declares for that output" and rule 3 says "a binding output [takes] the class the binding declares", but the decision says "a disclosure class only rises" and its invariant says "lowers_class(any construct) -> never".
open_points.question: When an operation receives a higher-class input but declares a lower-class output, does the output take the binding's declared class or retain the highest input class?
options: Use the binding output class even when it lowers the class
Use the maximum of the binding output class and all received input classes
Refuse a binding or flow that could lower the class
open_points.default_guess: Use the explicit binding-output rule, despite the only-rises invariant.

open_points.subject: A07 redacted failure-detail length
open_points.text: Rule 5 says a protected `failure_detail` is returned to an agent "only as its length and that class" but does not define the unit of length.
open_points.question: Is the disclosed length measured in Unicode scalar values, UTF-8 bytes, or the stored truncated detail's characters or bytes?
options: UTF-8 byte length of the stored truncated detail
Character count of the stored truncated detail
Length of the original detail before truncation
open_points.default_guess: Return the UTF-8 byte length of the stored truncated detail.

open_points.subject: A16 malformed request precedence
open_points.text: Rule 1 orders size, configuration/token, operation/schema, and authorization, but does not say how a token and operation are extracted when the request message is malformed, cannot be decoded, has duplicate envelope fields, or has a non-string token.
open_points.question: What refusal and precedence apply when the request cannot be parsed far enough to perform the token check?
options: Reject malformed framing or envelope immediately after the byte-size check
Treat an absent or unusable token as the uniform token refusal
Parse a minimal authentication envelope first, then validate the operation payload later
open_points.default_guess: After the size check, reject malformed framing or envelope before attempting authentication.

open_points.subject: A16 configuration re-read parsing
open_points.text: Rule 2 says the kernel re-reads the configuration and "takes from it only the token list", while its first re-read check says "the file can be read and parsed" and "Exactly four checks apply to a re-read".
open_points.question: Does a token-list re-read require the entire installation configuration to satisfy its schema, or only enough structure to parse and validate the token list?
options: Validate only the token-list portion and ignore all other changed fields until restart
Require the entire configuration schema to remain valid but apply only token-list changes
Parse any JSON object and extract a token list if present
open_points.default_guess: Validate only the token-list portion and leave every other field at its start-time value.

open_points.subject: A16 constant-time token comparison
open_points.text: Rules 1 and the formal invariant require tokens to be compared "in constant time", but configured tokens may have different lengths and the number of agent tokens is not fixed.
open_points.question: Constant with respect to which facts must authentication timing be independent: token contents, token length, matching position, and/or number of configured tokens?
options: Constant only with respect to equal-length token contents
Compare against every configured token without early exit, while length and token count may affect time
Require fixed-length tokens and a fixed or bounded comparison schedule
open_points.default_guess: Compare against every configured token without early exit and use a constant-time byte comparison for each candidate; permit length and configured-token count to affect time.

open_points.subject: A16 named-agent identity across configuration changes
open_points.text: M27 identifies an agent by `agent_name`; A16 refuses only two simultaneous tokens with one name, and allows the token list to be replaced between requests. Nothing says whether a removed name may later be reused or whether changing the token under a name preserves the same actor.
open_points.question: What makes a named agent the same principal across token rotation, removal, and later re-addition?
options: The name is the durable identity, so any later token under that name is the same agent
A name may be reused only for rotation of the same principal under an operational rule
A removed name can never be reused in an installation
Record an additional stable principal identifier
open_points.default_guess: Treat `agent_name` as the durable identity and token replacement under that name as rotation.

open_points.subject: A16 token length versus request string bound
open_points.text: Installation tokens have only a minimum of 43 characters, while rule 4 says "every other string anywhere in the request" is at most `bounded_text_bytes_max`; every request carries a token.
open_points.question: Is the authentication token subject to `bounded_text_bytes_max`, and if so must configured tokens also be capped so that a valid configured token cannot be unusable?
options: Exclude the authentication token from the generic request-string bound
Apply the bound to both configured and presented tokens
Allow longer configured tokens but reject their requests at schema validation
open_points.default_guess: Apply the same maximum to configured and presented tokens.

open_points.subject: A16 list ordering for mutable entities
open_points.text: Rule 6 says items come "newest first, in reverse store order" and discusses records whose status changes between pages, but bindings, approvals, grants, and runs are mutable entities with several store changes.
open_points.question: Which store position determines the list position and continuation boundary of a mutable entity: its creation, its latest transition, or a separate immutable listing record?
options: The entity's creation position never changes
The entity moves to the position of its latest state transition
Each transition is listed as a separate record
open_points.default_guess: Use the entity's creation position and never move it when its status changes.

open_points.subject: A16 fixed MCP operation inventory
open_points.text: K-11 names the fixed surface as "inspect, author, try, run, resume, read traces, and the owner's approve, accept, activate, grant, revoke, resolve and cancel", while the State 0 action table and A16 rule 3 additionally require distinct behavior for adding and capturing trial cases, releasing failed runs, rolling back slots, proposing bindings, and composing flows.
open_points.question: What exact typed MCP operations exist, and are the additional State 0 actions separate operations or variants hidden under the shorter K-11 verbs?
options: Expose one distinct operation for every State 0 action row
Group related actions under the K-11 verbs with tagged request variants
Treat K-11's list as non-exhaustive and let State 5 enumerate the exact surface
open_points.default_guess: Expose one distinct typed operation for every State 0 action row.

open_points.subject: A16 agent-name bounds
open_points.text: Agent names come from configuration and are written into durable Actor fields, but A16 bounds request strings only and gives no length, character-set, or count bound for configured agent names or agent tokens.
open_points.question: What configuration limits prevent unbounded actor names or an unbounded token list from entering authentication work and durable records?
options: Apply `bounded_text_bytes_max` to each agent name and define a release ceiling for token count
Allow arbitrary UTF-8 names and any token count subject only to available resources
Define separate release ceilings for names, tokens, and token-list cardinality
open_points.default_guess: Bound agent names by `bounded_text_bytes_max` and add a release-fixed maximum token count.

open_points.subject: A17 credential-file size
open_points.text: Rule 2 reads and decodes the secret file at request-build time, but gives no maximum byte size for that file or credential value.
open_points.question: At what size is a credential file refused as `credential_unresolved`, and is it read with a hard bound before allocation?
options: Use `bounded_text_bytes_max` as the credential-file and value limit
Define a separate release ceiling for credentials
Allow any size that fits available memory and the HTTP implementation
open_points.default_guess: Use `bounded_text_bytes_max` as a hard read limit.

open_points.subject: A17 credential newline, characters, and wire encoding
open_points.text: A credential is decoded as UTF-8 "without one trailing newline" and refused if it "holds ... a control character", then is added as an HTTP header value. The newline form, definition of control character, permitted non-ASCII characters, and wire encoding are not defined.
open_points.question: Exactly which trailing newline is removed, which Unicode or byte values are forbidden, and how is an accepted non-ASCII credential encoded on the wire?
options: Remove one LF only, reject ASCII controls including CR/LF, and require printable ASCII
Accept one LF or CRLF, reject Unicode control categories, and encode the value as UTF-8
Use the HTTP library's accepted field-value rules and map any rejection to `credential_unresolved`
open_points.default_guess: Remove one LF or one CRLF and require printable ASCII excluding controls.

open_points.subject: A17 secret-file path traversal and replacement
open_points.text: The secret path is absolute and is read "without following a symbolic link", but the text does not say whether this applies only to the final path component or to every component, nor which opened file is checked if the path is replaced during resolution.
open_points.question: Must every path component be opened without following symlinks, and must ownership, mode, and bytes all be checked and read from the same open file descriptor?
options: Reject symlinks in every path component and validate/read one opened descriptor
Reject only a symlink at the final component
Resolve parent symlinks but prohibit a final-component symlink
open_points.default_guess: Walk every component without following symlinks and validate and read the same descriptor.

open_points.subject: A17 selected manifest instance validity
open_points.text: The installation selects an instance "by its manifest instance name" and a service with no selected instance is not invocable, but no rule says what happens when the configured name is absent, duplicated in the manifest, or ceases to exist at the configured revision.
open_points.question: Does an invalid selected-instance name stop kernel startup, count as no selected instance, or become `instance_address_missing` only when that service is used?
options: Refuse kernel startup
Treat it as no selected instance and refuse binding proposal or send accordingly
Start successfully and report `instance_address_missing` at proposal or send time
open_points.default_guess: Start successfully and treat the service as having no selected instance.

open_points.subject: A17 secrets embedded in instance metadata
open_points.text: State 0 says service credentials live in protected installation configuration and never enter an answer, while A09 permits an absolute `api_base_url` with a host and A10 exposes the full URL and required-header values in approval previews. Neither text prohibits URL userinfo or secret values in manifest-required headers.
open_points.question: Are credentials or other secrets forbidden in `api_base_url` userinfo and required-header values, and how is that prohibition detected?
options: Reject URL userinfo and require manifest-required headers to be non-secret
Allow them and expose them as ordinary manifest data
Allow them but redact them using an explicit manifest secrecy marker
open_points.default_guess: Reject URL userinfo and treat required headers as non-secret configuration.

open_points.subject: A17 MCP listen address
open_points.text: The configuration contains "the address the kernel's one `mcp` entrance listens on, which the host's reverse proxy reaches", but no rule limits that address to a local interface or defines whether TCP, Unix sockets, wildcard addresses, and public interfaces are allowed.
open_points.question: Which listen-address forms are valid, and must the kernel prevent a configuration that exposes the MCP entrance outside the reverse proxy?
options: Permit only a loopback TCP address or a Unix-domain socket
Permit any syntactically valid address because the host configuration is trusted
Permit wildcard or public addresses only with an explicit installation flag
open_points.default_guess: Permit only loopback TCP addresses or Unix-domain sockets.

open_points.subject: A13 empty mapped operation output class
open_points.text: A13 rule 6 says an empty mapped node's output list "takes the highest class among the node's inputs", while A07 rule 3 and M21 say a binding output takes the class the binding declares.
open_points.question: For an empty mapped operation node, does each empty output list take the binding output's declared class or the highest class among the node's inputs?
options: Use the binding output's declared class
Use the highest input class
Use the maximum of the binding output class and highest input class
open_points.default_guess: Use the maximum, preserving the only-rises rule.

open_points.subject: A13 mapped node with failed and waiting elements
open_points.text: Rule 6 says "A mapped node concludes only when every element has concluded" and also "any failed element makes it failed for its dependants"; rule 8 says a run rests while some elements wait.
open_points.question: If one mapped element has failed while another is still waiting, do the mapped node's dependants become `upstream_failed` immediately, or do they wait until every element concludes?
options: Fail dependants immediately once any element fails
Wait for every element to conclude before failing dependants
Stop or cancel the remaining waiting elements when failure becomes certain
open_points.default_guess: Wait for all elements to conclude, then mark dependants `upstream_failed`.

open_points.subject: A13 ordering of ready execution versus derived non-execution records
open_points.text: Rule 2 orders ready node execution by smallest `node_id`; rules 4 and 5 create `skipped_by_guard` and `upstream_failed` conclusions; A15 orders nodes that "become non-executable together" but gives no precedence between writing those records and executing an independently ready node.
open_points.question: At each advancement step, are all newly derivable skip and upstream-failure records written before selecting a ready node, after ready nodes are exhausted, or interleaved in one common node-id order?
options: Reach a fixed point of derived skip/failure records before executing a ready node
Execute the smallest ready node first and derive non-executable records only when no node is ready
Choose the smallest node across both executable and derivably non-executable nodes
open_points.default_guess: Choose the smallest node across executable and derivably non-executable nodes.

open_points.subject: A13 mapped outputs when one aggregate exceeds the value limit
open_points.text: Rule 6 says each mapped value list is written "when the list is first delivered" and an oversized list makes "the node ... failed for its dependants", but does not say what happens to other output lists already derivable or deliverable from the same mapped node.
open_points.question: If one mapped output list fits and another exceeds `stored_value_bytes_max`, are any fitting outputs delivered or exposed as produced, or does the aggregate failure discard every output of that mapped node atomically?
options: Discard all mapped-node outputs atomically
Keep and report fitting outputs while failing only dependants of the oversized output
Keep fitting flow outputs but make all downstream nodes `upstream_failed`
open_points.default_guess: Discard all outputs atomically and fail every dependant of the mapped node.

open_points.subject: A13 node identifier ordering
open_points.text: A05 uses the empty string as the node identifier of a flow endpoint, while composition only refuses repeated node IDs and A13 selects the smallest `node_id`; no rule forbids a real node whose `node_id` is empty.
open_points.question: May a flow node have an empty `node_id`, and if so how is it ordered distinctly from flow input and output endpoints?
options: Forbid an empty node ID at composition
Allow it and add endpoint-kind as an ordering tie-breaker
Allow it to compare equal to flow endpoints
open_points.default_guess: Forbid an empty node ID at composition.

open_points.subject: Run finalization with failures and waits
open_points.text: M19 says "The run is `failed` when no node can run any more and some node failed", while A13 rule 7 ends a run only "When nothing can execute and nothing waits" and rule 8 rests a run while elements wait.
open_points.question: If a run has a failed branch and an independent element still waiting, does it end `failed` immediately or remain `awaiting_approval` or `pending` until the wait is resolved?
options: Remain waiting until no waiting point remains
End `failed` as soon as no node is currently executable
End failed and discard or void all remaining waits
open_points.default_guess: Remain waiting until every wait is resolved or the owner cancels or refuses the run.
